differences_found.description: Wrong lineage traced in the first draft of this verification
differences_found.root_cause: products_5k_enriched.json -> products_enriched.json also reconciles cleanly at 5000, which made it look like a plausible match, but it is v1.0's pipeline
differences_found.resolution: Caught in review; corrected to trace the real DB069 -> DB070 lineage named by validation_manifest.json's source field
differences_found.impact: None on the final counts reported here, which now reflect the real v1.1 chain end to end

differences_found.description: Raw SHA-256 of local foodremedy_release_v1.1.json does not match the manifest's stated hash on a Windows checkout
differences_found.root_cause: Git on Windows (core.autocrlf=true) converts LF line endings to CRLF on checkout, changing the file's raw bytes without changing its content
differences_found.resolution: Hash recomputed with line endings normalised back to LF matches the manifest and DB070's README exactly, confirming content identity
differences_found.corrected_framing: This is not a false DB068 failure. The integrity gate is correct to reject the raw, as-checked-out file, because its raw bytes genuinely differ from the approved artifact until normalised. The actionable gap is the repository's missing .gitattributes enforcing LF line endings for release JSON files - that is the fix, not a change to DB068's gate.
differences_found.impact: None on record counts or data integrity. Every Windows checkout will keep failing raw-hash verification, correctly, until .gitattributes is added.

result: PASS - raw 61,373 -> DB069 selection (5,000 included / 56,373 excluded) -> DB069 candidate (5,000) -> DB070 cleaning/enrichment (5,000) -> DB070 validation (5,000 valid, 0 invalid) -> final release (5,000) reconciles exactly at every stage, with zero unaccounted records

provenance.note: Raw/approved hash mismatch is a Windows line-ending (core.autocrlf) artifact; see differences_found for why this is not treated as a false integrity-gate failure
